=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Headline:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced." It collapses every protection into one low cap / short period / all-claims regime, relies on blanket data-room disclosure plus a constructive-knowledge bar, and pushes three cash items (Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k, Ironquay AUD 180k) past Completion or off the funds flow despite a debt-free/cash-free price. Useful point in our favour: the Seller's own Disclosure Letter concedes that the Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay assignment and DD-006 investigation are all incomplete.

---

**SPA-N-001 – General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- Buyer wants: 50% (AUD 12m), floor at 30% (AUD 7.2m); cap applies to general warranties only.
- Recommend: Counter at 50%, settle no lower than 30%. *Reason: with 30% of revenue hanging on one customer and open IP/privacy issues, 20% leaves most realistic loss scenarios uncovered.*

**SPA-N-002 – De minimis & basket**
- Seller: AUD 25k per claim; AUD 250k deductible basket (excess only).
- Buyer wants: AUD 10k de minimis; AUD 150k–240k *tipping* basket (first dollar recoverable); related/series claims aggregated; no thresholds for fundamental, tax, specific indemnities.
- Recommend: Tipping basket at ~1% (AUD 240k), de minimis AUD 10k, aggregation language. *Reason: a deductible basket is a hidden further price concession and the Sandbar split (3 × AUD 110k) shows why aggregation matters.*

**SPA-N-003 – General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months; limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: 24 months general (two audit cycles); separate periods elsewhere (see N-004, N-016).
- Recommend: 24 months, with claims notified in-period surviving until resolved. *Reason: 18 months often expires before the first full post-Completion audit surfaces issues.*

**SPA-N-004 – Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18 months.
- Buyer wants: 100% of price, 7 years (or unlimited), no de minimis/basket.
- Recommend: Reject outright. *Reason: if title fails the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing; a 20% cap on that is unacceptable at any price.*

**SPA-N-005 – Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" – no fraud carve-out.
- Buyer wants: express carve-out for fraud, wilful misconduct, wilful concealment and dishonesty of Seller, Company or their officers, from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
- Recommend: Insert carve-out as a non-negotiable. *Reason: market-standard, and a non-reliance clause with no fraud carve-out is both unreasonable and a litigation trap.*

**SPA-N-006 – Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records"; cl 1.4 admits nothing.
- Buyer wants: only matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter (specific, with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify nature and scope); no blanket data-room/public-record disclosure; public searches limited to specified ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia searches on a stated date; cut-off date confirmed and no post-signing disclosure updates that reduce claim rights.
- Recommend: Reject general disclosure; require fair-disclosure standard. *Reason: a data room you cannot fully verify in time is not disclosure, it is a warranty wipe-out.*

**SPA-N-007 – Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: cl 8.3 bars claims for anything the Buyer or advisers knew or that was "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- Buyer wants: delete; at most, bar limited to the *actual* knowledge of 2–3 named deal team members of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, excluding adviser knowledge and anything "discoverable."
- Recommend: Delete cl 8.3 (fallback: named-individuals actual knowledge). *Reason: "discoverable" + general disclosure means no warranty claim ever succeeds.*

**SPA-N-008 – Bluefen consent (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% revenue)**
- Seller: "reasonable endeavours"; consent "treated as satisfied" on delivery of written consent; Disclosure Letter confirms no consent and no evidence cl 11.3 conditions met.
- Buyer wants: condition precedent to Completion – unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 *and* evidence cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, in form reasonably satisfactory to Buyer; Seller "all reasonable/best endeavours"; Buyer waiver right; long-stop date; termination if not met; warranty of no Bluefen termination/renegotiation.
- Recommend: Hard CP, Buyer sign-off on form. *Reason: losing 30% of revenue post-Completion with no price adjustment is the single largest value risk in the deal.*

**SPA-N-009 – Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m)**
- Seller: release "to be provided following Completion."
- Buyer wants: repayment at Completion from the purchase price (funds flow item), executed deed of release, PPSR discharge and return of any share/guarantee security *delivered at Completion*; payout letter with exact figure ≥5 business days pre-Completion; change-of-control under cl 8.1 addressed.
- Recommend: Insist on at-Completion payoff and release as a Completion deliverable. *Reason: debt-free/cash-free means the Buyer does not inherit a AUD 3.2m secured facility on trust that a release will arrive later.*

**SPA-N-010 – Employee bonuses (AUD 420k)**
- Seller: "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow.
- Buyer wants: treat as Transaction Expense/Debt – deducted from price with grossed-up super, payroll tax and on-costs (budget c. AUD 480–500k); itemised in funds flow; Seller indemnity for any shortfall; confirm no accelerated vesting/other change-of-control triggers.
- Recommend: Price deduction plus indemnity. *Reason: the Company (now the Buyer's) pays these after Completion; if they are not in the funds flow the Buyer funds them.*

**SPA-N-011 – Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k); "adequate."
- Buyer wants: CP/Completion deliverable – proof of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay; specific indemnity for all loss from any defect in title to Project Materials (not just the fee), outside basket/de minimis, separate cap (suggest 100% of price or at least the value attributable to the product), 6-year period.
- Recommend: Fix pre-Completion, backstop with a broad specific indemnity. *Reason: AUD 180k is the fee, not the loss – the loss is not owning the code.*

**SPA-N-012 – Export/privacy incident (DD-006, ~1,240 records)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter," not material; no breach admitted, no loss amount.
- Buyer wants: Seller to complete investigation and deliver findings pre-Completion (including whether Privacy Act NDB notification to OAIC/individuals is required); specific indemnity for notification costs, regulatory penalties, third-party claims and remediation, outside thresholds and the general cap; warranty of no other incidents; Buyer approval of any notification/regulator correspondence.
- Recommend: Specific indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation covenant. *Reason: an unresolved notifiable-data-breach exposure cannot be left to a 20%-capped, data-room-disclosed warranty.*

**SPA-N-013 – Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k)**
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs.
- Buyer wants: confirmation whether each is already committed/accrued, terminable, and whether the three are one arrangement split in three; any amount committed pre-Completion but benefiting the Seller's period treated via working-capital/Debt adjustment; warranty that no contracts have been structured to fall below disclosure/threshold levels.
- Recommend: Price-adjust if accrued; otherwise obtain warranted specific disclosure. *Reason: the Seller's own letter cannot say whether they are unavoidable or ordinary-course, so neither can the Buyer accept them as such.*

**SPA-N-014 – Category separation**
- Seller: one limitation regime for all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: distinct regimes – (a) General warranties: 30–50% / 24 months; (b) Fundamental (title, capacity): 100% / 7 years; (c) Tax: 100% / later of 7 years and expiry of ATO amendment period + 6 months; (d) IP/Data: elevated cap, 4–6 years; (e) Specific indemnities, Leakage, covenants and Completion obligations: not subject to caps, thresholds or warranty time limits; fraud carved out of everything.
- Recommend: Redraft cl 12–13 into a limitations schedule by category. *Reason: "all claims unless stated otherwise" is designed to sweep indemnities and fundamental claims into the weakest regime.*

**SPA-N-015 – Title verification**
- Seller: title "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012; letter concedes Buyer has not verified.
- Buyer wants: independent ASIC company and PPSR searches (shares and all-assets – note Riverlark security), original share certificates, register inspection, director/secretary certificate at Completion; warranties that Seller is sole legal and beneficial owner free of all Encumbrances, register is accurate, no options/convertibles/pre-emption rights; executed transfers and Harbourglass board approval.
- Recommend: Run searches now and add full title deliverables. *Reason: a company-maintained register is Seller-controlled evidence, not verification.*

**SPA-N-016 – Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: "settled under the general regime" (20% / 18 months / data-room disclosed).
- Buyer wants: standalone Tax Indemnity (all pre-Completion tax, pound-for-pound, 100% cap, limitation per N-014, straddle-period rules, Seller conduct of pre-Completion audits with Buyer consent rights); full IP warranties (ownership of all Company IP, no third-party claims, all developer/contractor assignments including Ironquay, open-source compliance) with elevated cap and longer period; data/privacy warranties aligned to N-012.
- Recommend: Reject "settled"; table Buyer's tax indemnity and IP/data warranty schedule. *Reason: tax is the one area where liabilities surface years later and the Ironquay facts already show the IP chain is not clean.*

---

**Suggested priority for the mark-up:** (1) N-008 Bluefen CP, (2) N-009 Riverlark at Completion, (3) N-004/N-014 separate fundamental & tax regimes, (4) N-005 fraud carve-out, (5) N-006/N-007 disclosure and knowledge, (6) N-010/N-011/N-013 price adjustments, (7) N-012 privacy indemnity, (8) N-001/N-002/N-003 commercial caps. Items 1–5 are structural and should be positioned as conditions of proceeding; items 6–8 are tradeable.

Note: this is a negotiation analysis, not formal legal advice; NSW-law drafting and Privacy Act notification positions should be confirmed by external counsel before the mark-up issues.
